description: Encode multi-site mutation optimization as a QUBO problem and solve with simulated quantum annealing on classical hardware. Binary variables represent mutation inclusion, pairwise terms encode epistasis. This bridges quantum computing research with protein engineering.
mathematical_formalization: Binary x_{i,a} = 1 if position i has amino acid a. QUBO: min H = sum h_{i,a} * x_{i,a} + sum J_{(i,a),(j,b)} * x_{i,a} * x_{j,b}, subject to sum_a x_{i,a} = 1. h from single-mutant ddG, J from pairwise epistasis. Solve via simulated annealing with transverse field.
analogical_connections: Mohseni et al. (2024): ML + quantum annealing for protein design outperforms conventional optimization classically
Ising model spin glasses: mutations = spins, stability = ground state energy
VLSI circuit placement: components on silicon map to residues in protein
implementation_hypothesis: Encode k positions * 20 states as k*20 binary variables with one-hot constraints. Set h from ESM-2, J from double-mutant screen or GNN. Run simulated annealing with parallel tempering (16 replicas, 10K sweeps). Also try D-Wave neal sampler.
experiment_seed: Formulate QUBO for 30 Mega-scale proteins with k=6. Compare SA, parallel tempering, neal vs beam search and MCTS. Measure best ddG, time, and solution diversity.
